nodes.title: Algebra, functions and graphs
nodes.summary: School algebra: equations, powers, logarithms, functions, graphs, and proportions. It is needed for chemical kinetics, statistics, physiological models, and machine learning.

nodes.title: Mathematical analysis
nodes.summary: Limits, derivatives, integrals, and continuous change. Forms a language for reaction kinetics, population dynamics, optimization and differential models.

nodes.title: Linear algebra
nodes.summary: Vectors, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, and matrix decompositions. A shared prerequisite for multi-omics, ML, network models, and image analysis.

nodes.title: Probability and statistics
nodes.summary: Random values, distributions, estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing. Reused in all experimental, clinical and computational branches.

resources.title: MIT 18.05 Introduction to Probability and Statistics

nodes.title: Differential equations and dynamical systems
nodes.summary: Models of change over time, stability, feedback and nonlinear dynamics. Necessary for signaling networks, cell populations, pharmacokinetics and systemic physiology.

nodes.title: Discrete mathematics and graph theory
nodes.summary: Combinatorics, graphs, recurrence relations, and proofs. Required for biological networks, knowledge graphs, lineage trees, and graph ML models.

nodes.title: School physics and energy
nodes.summary: Mechanics, energy, electricity, diffusion, waves and basic thermodynamics. Supports biophysics, imaging, electrophysiology and transport phenomena.

nodes.title: General chemistry
nodes.summary: Atomic structure, chemical bonds, stoichiometry, equilibrium, acids and bases, thermodynamics and kinetics. Basis for biochemistry, pharmacology and materials science.

nodes.title: Organic chemistry
nodes.summary: Structure and reactivity of organic molecules, functional groups, stereochemistry and reaction mechanisms. It is necessary for biochemistry and medicinal chemistry.

nodes.title: School biology
nodes.summary: Cell, heredity, evolution, metabolism, physiology and ecology. The starting point for all longevity biological routes.

resources.title: Khan Academy: Preparing to study biology

nodes.title: Fundamentals of programming
nodes.summary: Variables, conditionals, loops, functions, data structures, and debugging. A foundation for data analysis, bioinformatics, ML, and experiment automation.

nodes.title: Scientific thinking and working with evidence
nodes.summary: Hypotheses, causality, controls, reproducibility, sources of error, and levels of evidence. Protects the map from conflating correlations, preclinical results, and clinical efficacy.

resources.title: NIH Training for Rigor and Reproducibility

nodes.title: Introductory university biology
nodes.summary: A unified framework of biochemistry, genetics, molecular and cellular biology with an emphasis on the mechanisms of living systems and experimental evidence.

nodes.title: Biochemistry
nodes.summary: Protein structure and function, enzymes, membranes, metabolism, bioenergetics, and molecular recognition. The shared language of most molecular longevity research.

nodes.title: Molecular biology
nodes.summary: DNA replication and repair, transcription, RNA processing, gene translation and regulation. Needed for genome maintenance, editing, omics and reprogramming.

nodes.title: Cell biology
nodes.summary: Organelles, membrane transport, cytoskeleton, cell cycle, signaling, apoptosis, and tissue cellular organization. The basis of senescence, autophagy and regenerative medicine.

nodes.title: Genetics and genomics
nodes.summary: Inheritance, recombination, linkage, population variation, genome structure, and genotype-phenotype connections. Comparative biology, cancer evolution and genome editing.

nodes.title: Epigenetics and chromatin
nodes.summary: DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, 3D genome and cellular inheritance. Central base for aging clocks, epigenome editing and reprogramming.

resources.title: The Nature of Epigenetic Aging from a Single-Cell Perspective

nodes.title: Physiology and homeostasis
nodes.summary: Organ functions, endocrine and neural control, blood circulation, respiration, kidneys, exchange and inter-organ coordination. It is necessary for the transition from cellular effects to whole-body outcomes.

nodes.title: Immunology
nodes.summary: Innate and adaptive immunity, antigen presentation, tolerance, inflammation, immune memory and tumor surveillance. Base for inflammaging, thymus/HSC and cancer proofing.

nodes.title: Microbiology and Microbial Ecology
nodes.summary: Bacterial physiology, communities, host-microbe interactions, ecology, and microbial metabolism. The basis for the causal study of microbiome and dysbiosis.

nodes.title: Developmental and stem cell biology
nodes.summary: Cell fate, differentiation, morphogens, stem-cell niches, regeneration and iPSC. Common base for tissue repair, organoids, HSC and partial reprogramming.

resources.title: MIT 7.013 Introductory Biology — development and stem cells readings

nodes.title: Neuroscience
nodes.summary: Neurons and glia, synapses, circuits, myelin, neurovascular unit and plasticity. Brain aging, microglia and neural replacement.

nodes.title: Cancer Biology and Tumor Evolution
nodes.summary: Oncogenes, tumor suppressors, genome instability, clonal evolution, microenvironment, immune escape and metastasis. Mandatory safety pre-requisite for telomerase, reprogramming and regeneration.

nodes.title: Geroscience and Hallmarks of Aging
nodes.summary: Integrative model of mechanisms of aging, their relationships and criteria of causality. Provides top-level navigation, but does not prove the effectiveness of specific therapies.

resources.title: Hallmarks of Aging: An Expanding Universe
USC PhD in Biology of Aging Curriculum
resources.provider: USC Leonard Davis School of Gerontology / Buck Institute

nodes.title: Metabolism, Bioenergetics and Redox
nodes.summary: Glycolysis, TCA, oxidative phosphorylation, NAD/NADH, ROS, nutrient sensing and metabolic flux. Common base for mTOR/AMPK, NAD+, mitochondria and cancer metabolism.

resources.title: NAD in Aging Biology: Potential Applications and Many Unknowns

nodes.title: Proteostasis, autophagy and lysosomes
nodes.summary: Protein folding, chaperones, ubiquitin-proteasome system, macroautophagy, CMA and lysosomal degradation. Required for protein aggregates, lipofuscin and mitophagy.

resources.title: Mechanisms of Autophagy–Lysosome Dysfunction in Neurodegenerative Diseases

nodes.title: Mitochondrial biology and quality control
nodes.summary: Electron transport, mtDNA, dynamics, biogenesis, unfolded-protein response and mitophagy. Allows you to distinguish energy defects, signaling and removal of damaged organelles.

resources.title: Suppressed Basal Mitophagy Drives Cellular Aging Phenotypes

nodes.title: Cellular senescence
nodes.summary: Stable cell-cycle arrest, SASP, biomarkers, beneficial and pathological roles, heterogeneity and immune clearance. Common base for senolytics, senomorphics and senescence-aware safety.

resources.title: Roles of Chromatin and Genome Instability in Cellular Senescence

nodes.title: Extracellular matrix and mechanobiology
nodes.summary: Collagen, elastin, proteoglycans, cross-links, matrix turnover, stiffness, mechanotransduction and fibrosis. ECM rejuvenation, AGE and tissue engineering.

resources.title: Strategic Outline of Interventions Targeting Extracellular Matrix

nodes.title: Pharmacology and toxicology
nodes.summary: Dose-response, receptors, ADME, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic window and safety. Mandatory before developing or interpreting gerotherapeutics.

nodes.title: Systems biology and biological networks
nodes.summary: Pathways, feedback loops, network motifs, multi-scale models and emergent behavior. It connects individual hallmarks and is needed for combination therapies.

resources.title: EMBL-EBI Methods in Bioinformatics: Biological Networks

nodes.title: Python and data analysis
nodes.summary: Python, NumPy, pandas, notebooks, testing and tabular data processing. A common practical node for bioinformatics, ML, statistics and automation.

nodes.title: Algorithms and data structures
nodes.summary: Complexity, arrays, hash tables, trees, graphs, and algorithmic design. It is necessary for scalable processing of omics and knowledge graphs.

nodes.title: Linux, Git and Reproducible Computing
nodes.summary: Command Prompt, version control, environments, containers, tests, and provenance computing. Makes analysis testable and repeatable.

nodes.title: Scientific Data Management and FAIR
nodes.summary: Metadata, identifiers, formats, ontologies, repositories, privacy and FAIR principles. Needed for large cohorts, multi-omics and results sharing.

resources.title: EMBL-EBI: Bringing Data to Life — Data Management

nodes.title: Experimental design and biostatistics
nodes.summary: Controls, randomization, blinding, power, sample size, repeated measures, multiple testing and effect sizes. It is mandatory to evaluate any intervention of longevity.

nodes.title: Causal inference
nodes.summary: Confounding, DAGs, counterfactuals, target trial emulation and causal estimands. It helps distinguish the biomarker association from the causal mechanism or effect of the intervention.

resources.title: Causal Inference: What If
resources.provider: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

nodes.title: Systematic reviews and meta-analysis
nodes.summary: Question formulation, research search, risk of bias, synthesis, GRADE and interpretation of uncertainty. You need to check claims in fast-changing longevity.

resources.title: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions

nodes.title: Clinical research and trials
nodes.summary: Protocol design, endpoints, randomization, monitoring, adverse events, ethics and regulatory context. It is necessary to translate geroscience from models to humans.

resources.title: NIH Introduction to the Principles and Practice of Clinical Research

nodes.title: Bioethics and regulation
nodes.summary: Human subjects, informed consent, germline issues, gene therapy oversight, animal welfare, data privacy and dual-use risk. Necessary for secure broadcasting of frontier technologies.

nodes.title: Practical molecular biology
nodes.summary: Pipetting, nucleic-acid purification, PCR, cloning, electrophoresis, quantitative assays and lab records. Basic wet-lab competence for genome and gene-expression research.

nodes.title: Cell Culture and Functional Assays
nodes.summary: Aseptic technique, primary/immortalized cells, organotypic models, viability, proliferation, senescence and perturbation assays. It is necessary for preclinical testing of interventions.

nodes.title: Microscopy, imaging and flow cytometry
nodes.summary: Optical microscopy, fluorescence, image quantification, flow cytometry and sorting. Allows measurement of cell states, immune populations and tissue phenotypes.

nodes.title: Model organisms and aging research
nodes.summary: Yeast, worms, flies, fish and mice; lifespan/healthspan assays, strain/sex effects, welfare and translational limits. It is necessary for correct reading of preclinical results.

nodes.title: Assay development and high-throughput screening
nodes.summary: Assay quality, controls, Z-prime, dose-response, automation and hit validation. CRISPR/drug screens and search for senolytics or pathway modulators.

nodes.title: Basics of bioinformatics
nodes.summary: Biological databases, sequence analysis, annotation, workflows and reproducibility. It combines molecular biology with computational analysis.

resources.title: EMBL-EBI Competency Hub and Career Profiles

nodes.title: NGS and analysis of genomic variants
nodes.summary: Sequencing technologies, QC, alignment, variant calling, annotation and interpretation. Somatic mutations, CRISPR screens and comparative genomics.

resources.title: EMBL-EBI Methods in Bioinformatics — Genomic Variants

nodes.title: Transcriptomics and gene expression analysis
nodes.summary: RNA-seq design, normalization, differential expression, pathway enrichment and confounders. Required for aging signatures, perturbations and reprogramming.

resources.title: RNA-seq Analysis Is Easy as 1-2-3 with Limma, Glimma and edgeR

nodes.title: Single-cell and spatial omics
nodes.summary: Experimental design, QC, dimensionality reduction, cell annotation, batch correction, trajectories and spatial context. Tissue-specific aging and rejuvenation atlases.

nodes.title: Proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics
nodes.summary: Mass spectrometry, feature identification, normalization, pathway analysis and measurement uncertainty. It is necessary for proteostasis, metabolism, biomarkers and multi-omics.

resources.title: EMBL-EBI Methods in Bioinformatics — Mass Spectrometry Proteomics

nodes.title: Integration of multi-omics
nodes.summary: Joint analysis of genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and microbiome, taking into account batch, missingness and different scales.

resources.title: Nonlinear Dynamics of Multi-Omics Profiles during Human Aging

nodes.title: Comparative biology and phylogenetic methods
nodes.summary: Phylogenetic trees, comparative models, orthology, convergent evolution and cross-species omics. It is necessary to search for natural mechanisms of longevity without pseudoreplication of species.

nodes.title: Structural biology and computational chemistry
nodes.summary: Protein structure, binding, molecular dynamics, docking and free-energy reasoning. AI protein design and structure-based drug discovery.

nodes.title: Computational analysis of bioimages
nodes.summary: Segmentation, tracking, feature extraction, quality control and deep-learning microscopy. Required for senescence, histology, organoids and high-content screening.

nodes.title: Basics of machine learning
nodes.summary: Supervised/unsupervised learning, train/validation/test, regularization, leakage, metrics and error analysis. Common base for clocks, omics, imaging and drug discovery.

nodes.title: Deep learning
nodes.summary: Neural networks, backpropagation, optimization, convolution, representation learning and uncertainty. Imaging, foundation models and generative design.

nodes.title: Transformers and large language models
nodes.summary: Attention, pretraining, tokenization, fine-tuning, retrieval, evaluation and failure modes. It is used for biomedical NLP but does not replace primary source testing.

resources.title: Stanford CS224N: NLP with Deep Learning

nodes.title: Biomedical NLP and knowledge graphs
nodes.summary: Entity normalization, relation extraction, ontologies, RAG, provenance and expert validation. Applied to literature mining and building a verifiable knowledge map.

resources.title: Large Language Models for Biomedicine: Best Practices
resources.provider: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association

nodes.title: Foundation models for cells and biological sequences
nodes.summary: Transformer-like models for single-cell, DNA, RNA and protein data; pretraining, transfer and benchmarking against simple baselines.

resources.title: Large-Scale Foundation Model on Single-Cell Transcriptomics
Gene Perturbation Prediction Does Not Yet Outperform Linear Baselines

nodes.title: Machine-learning aging clocks
nodes.summary: Building and validating clocks from methylation, omics, imaging, and clinical data; calibration, external validation, and distinction between prediction and causal aging.

resources.title: Epigenetic Ageing Clocks: Statistical Methods and Challenges

nodes.title: AI for Target Identification and Drug Discovery
nodes.summary: Representation learning, virtual screening, generative chemistry, ADMET prediction and prospective validation. A model score is not a substitute for experimental and clinical validation.

resources.title: Creating an AI-First Drug Discovery Engine

nodes.title: AI protein structure and design
nodes.summary: Structure prediction, sequence generation, binder design, protein language models and wet-lab validation. Applies to enzymes, biologics, sensors and repair tools.

nodes.title: Laboratory automation and active learning
nodes.summary: Robotics, liquid handling, experiment scheduling, Bayesian optimization, closed-loop design-test-learn and provenance-complete execution.

resources.title: Self-Driving Laboratories for Protein Fitness Landscapes

nodes.title: Validation and Security of Biomedical AI
nodes.summary: Dataset shift, leakage, bias, calibration, uncertainty, human evaluation, audit trails and adversarial/poisoning risks. A mandatory node before using AI in clinical and evidence workflows.

resources.title: QUEST Framework for Human Evaluation of Healthcare LLMs
Poisoning Medical Knowledge Using Large Language Models

nodes.title: Modeling and systems pharmacology
nodes.summary: Mechanistic models, PK/PD, network simulations, parameter fitting, sensitivity and uncertainty. Combination therapy and multi-target intervention planning.

resources.title: MIT 20.320 Analysis of Biomolecular and Cellular Systems

nodes.title: CRISPR and genome editing
nodes.summary: CRISPR-Cas nucleases, base/prime editing, guide design, delivery, off-target analysis and functional screens. A platform for gene testing and targeted therapeutic interventions.

resources.title: CRISPR–Cas9 Screens Reveal Regulators of Ageing in Neural Stem Cells

nodes.title: Gene therapy and delivery
nodes.summary: AAV/lentiviral vectors, non-viral nanoparticles, tissue tropism, expression control, immunogenicity, manufacturing and biodistribution. The main bottleneck of system genetic interventions.

nodes.title: Epigenome editing
nodes.summary: dCas-targeted activation/repression and record methylation/chromatin marks without breaking DNA. Used for causal tests and potential gene-expression recovery programs.

resources.title: Epigenome Editing Technologies for Discovery and Medicine

nodes.title: Synthetic biology and gene circuits
nodes.summary: Design-build-test-learn, promoters, sensors, logic gates, feedback, kill switches and engineered cells/microbes. A platform for monitoring and conditional response to damage states.

resources.title: Synthetic Macromolecular Switches for Therapeutic Cells

nodes.title: Protein engineering
nodes.summary: Directed evolution, rational design, library screening, affinity/specificity, stability and developmentability. Enzymes, binders, biologics and synthetic repair systems.

resources.title: MIT 20.109 Laboratory Fundamentals in Biological Engineering

nodes.title: Drug discovery and development
nodes.summary: Target validation, hit discovery, lead optimization, ADME/Tox, preclinical models, CMC and clinical development. Turns the mechanism into a testable drug intervention.

nodes.title: iPSC, differentiation and organoids
nodes.summary: Reprogramming to pluripotency, directed differentiation, organoid self-organization, maturation and disease modeling. Tissue replacement and humanized aging models.

resources.title: A Framework for Neural Organoids, Assembloids and Transplantation Studies

nodes.title: Tissue engineering and biomaterials
nodes.summary: Scaffolds, hydrogels, mechanics, cell-material interactions, vascularization and bioreactors. It is necessary for the growth and integration of functional tissues.

resources.title: MIT Tissue Engineering and Organ Regeneration

nodes.title: 3D bioprinting and biofabrication
nodes.summary: Bioinks, printing modalities, spatial patterning, organoid building blocks, perfusion and quality control. Active platform, but whole-organ manufacturing remains immature.

resources.title: Organoid Bioprinting: From Cells to Functional Tissues

nodes.title: Transplantation immunology and xenobiology
nodes.summary: Rejection, tolerance, immunosuppression, donor engineering, zoonotic risk, surgery and graft monitoring. Organ replacement and xenotransplantation.

resources.title: Design and Testing of a Humanized Porcine Donor

nodes.title: Cryobiology and organ preservation
nodes.summary: Ice formation, vitrification, cryoprotectant toxicity, perfusion, thermal stress and nanowarming. Real transplant-enabling area; whole-body revival not shown

resources.title: Organ Preservation: History, Advancements, and Perspectives

nodes.title: Immune-cell engineering
nodes.summary: Engineered T/NK/macrophage cells, receptors, logic gates, persistence, exhaustion and safety switches. Potentially applied to cancer surveillance and senescent-cell clearance.

resources.title: Synthetic Macromolecular Switches for Precision Control of Therapeutic Cells

nodes.title: Development and Validation of Biomarkers
nodes.summary: Analytical validity, biological validity, prognostic value, responsiveness, external replication and clinical utility. It is mandatory before using clocks as endpoints.

nodes.title: Design of combinations and multi-intervention trials
nodes.summary: Interaction models, dose/schedule optimization, factorial/adaptive designs, safety constraints and component attribution. It is necessary for the transition from individual repairs to a system set of interventions.

nodes.title: Metabolic interventions and nutrient sensing
nodes.summary: Research on mTOR, AMPK, insulin/IGF-1, sirtuins, caloric restriction mimetics, and the relationship of nutrient state to growth, autophagy, and repair.
nodes.evidence_note: The pathways are causally related to lifespan in model organisms; individual interventions have been investigated in humans, but human life extension and general rejuvenation have not been proven.

resources.title: Hallmarks of Aging: Deregulated Nutrient Sensing
Aging in Heart Failure: Biology over Chronology

nodes.title: NAD+ and redox restoration
nodes.summary: NAD biosynthesis/consumption, redox state, PARP, sirtuins and tissue-specific effects of NAD precursors.
nodes.evidence_note: Precursors increase NAD in humans, but the clinical effects of healthy aging are generally limited and ambiguous.

resources.title: NAD+ Precursor Supplementation in Human Ageing
NAD in Aging Biology: Potential Applications and Many Unknowns

nodes.title: Senolytics and senomorphics
nodes.summary: Selective destruction of senescent cells, suppression of SASP and immune-mediated clearance, taking into account the heterogeneity and useful roles of senescence.
nodes.evidence_note: The preclinical causal base is strong, but human studies are early; specificity, toxicity, and biomarkers selection remain challenges.

resources.title: How to Kill the Zombie Cells That Make You Age

nodes.title: Proteostasis restoration and removal of intracellular debris
nodes.summary: Enhance chaperones, proteasome, autophagy/lysosomes and remove protein aggregates or hard-to-destruct cargo, including lipofuscin-like damage.
nodes.evidence_note: Loss of proteostasis and disabled macroautophagy are established hallmarks; safe systemic enhancement and clearance of different aggregates require disease- and tissue-specific solutions.

nodes.title: Mitochondrial rejuvenation and mitophagy
nodes.summary: Restoration of mitochondrial quality through biogenesis, fusion/fission, mtDNA maintenance, redox control and removal of damaged organelles.
nodes.evidence_note: Mitochondrial dysfunction is causally associated with aging, but there is no universal therapy for different tissues; most intervention evidence is preclinical.

resources.title: Suppressed Basal Mitophagy Drives Cellular Aging Phenotypes

nodes.title: Genome maintenance and somatic clone control
nodes.summary: DNA repair, replication stress, somatic mutation detection, clonal hematopoiesis, lineage dynamics and prevention of pathological clonal expansion.
nodes.evidence_note: The accumulation of mutations and clonal expansion are established, but the safe control of all tissues and the causal contribution of different clones remain open challenges.

resources.title: Somatic Mutations and Drivers of Clonal Hematopoiesis

nodes.title: Telomere restoration and telomerase therapy
nodes.summary: Study of telomere attrition, telomerase/ALT, replicative senescence and tissue-specific telomere repair capabilities.
nodes.evidence_note: Telomere attrition is a hallmark, but telomerase supports replicative immortality of tumors; systemic activation requires strict cancer control.

resources.title: Targeting Telomeres: Telomere Maintenance and Cancer

nodes.title: Partial reprogramming and epigenetic rejuvenation
nodes.summary: Transient reprogramming factors, chemical reprogramming and targeted epigenome changes to restore a young cell state without loss of identity.
nodes.evidence_note: There are rejuvenation phenotypes in cells and mice; delivery, dedifferentiation, tissue-specific lethality and oncogenic risk are not solved, human rejuvenation is not proven.

resources.title: Mechanisms and Strategies for Rejuvenation through Epigenetic Reprogramming
Partial Cellular Reprogramming: A Deep Dive

nodes.title: Inflammaging, immunosenescence, HSC and thymus rejuvenation
nodes.summary: Chronic inflammation, myeloid bias, T-cell repertoire, thymic epithelial cells, HSC quality and immune surveillance recovery.
nodes.evidence_note: Immune aging is established; depleting myeloid-biased HSC and thymus regeneration are promising in models, but systemic human rejuvenation is not shown.

resources.title: Age-Related Epithelial Defects Limit Thymic Regeneration

nodes.title: Microbiome manipulation for healthy aging
nodes.summary: Host-microbe interactions, barrier integrity, microbial metabolites, diet, phages/probiotics and causal intervention design.
nodes.evidence_note: Dysbiosis is a hallmark, but associations depend on environment and health; transferability between cohorts is limited and causality remains difficult to establish.

resources.title: The Human Gut Microbiome and Aging

nodes.title: Systemic rejuvenation and circulating factors
nodes.summary: Endocrine, immune and extracellular-vesicle signals, plasma exchange and parabiosis models of interstitial aging.
nodes.evidence_note: Parabiosis shows systemic effects of blood in animals, but the specific mechanisms and clinical efficacy of young plasma have not been established.

resources.title: Aging Insights from Heterochronic Parabiosis Models

nodes.title: Stem-cell rejuvenation and regenerative signaling
nodes.summary: Aged stem-cell niches, quiescence/activation, lineage bias, Wnt/Notch/TGF-β and tissue regenerative function restoration.
nodes.evidence_note: Tissue-specific stem-cell defects are established; general activation of regeneration carries risks of aberrant differentiation, fibrosis, and cancer.

resources.title: Cellular Rejuvenation: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Interventions

nodes.title: Cell competition and selective replacement
nodes.summary: Using fitness differences to remove damaged cells and gradually populate tissues with more functional cells.
nodes.evidence_note: The fundamental biology is active, but therapeutic manipulation may select tumor-like cheaters; safe tissue replacement has not been demonstrated.

resources.title: Cell Competition and the Regulation of Protein Homeostasis

nodes.title: ECM rejuvenation, cross-links, AGE and fibrosis
nodes.summary: Matrix turnover, collagen/elastin damage, glycation cross-links, proteolysis, mechanotransduction and organ-specific fibrosis reversal.
nodes.evidence_note: ECM aging is recognized as important, but there is no universal cross-link breaker or method for systemic matrix renewal; the field remains underexplored.

resources.title: Strategic Outline of ECM Interventions for Healthy Longevity

nodes.title: Vascular rejuvenation and atherosclerosis reversal
nodes.summary: Endothelium, lipid retention, inflammation, senescence, thrombosis, plaque imaging, and disease-specific vascular repair.
nodes.evidence_note: The management of cardiovascular risk and individual forms of plaque regression are clinically feasible; the complete elimination of accumulated vascular damage remains an immature goal.

nodes.title: Cancer-proofing and tumor surveillance
nodes.summary: Genome stability, early detection, immune surveillance, engineered immune cells and safety constraints for regenerative and reprogramming therapies.
nodes.evidence_note: Cancer control is mandatory for radical longevity, but there is no single cancer-proofing technology; the mechanisms depend on tissue and tumor evolution.

resources.title: Peto's Paradox and Natural Cancer Resistance

nodes.title: Comparative longevity biology
nodes.summary: Comparison of long-lived species to search for convergent mechanisms of DNA repair, proteostasis, metabolism, and cancer resistance.
nodes.evidence_note: Active discovery; transfer of candidate mechanisms to humans requires causal functional validation.

resources.title: Peto's Paradox: Natural Strategies for Long Lifespans

nodes.title: Gene therapy and synthetic biology for longevity
nodes.summary: Tissue-specific delivery of genes/epigenetic regulators, engineered sensors, circuits and therapeutic cells to control damage pathways.
nodes.evidence_note: Enabling technologies are clinically real in individual diseases, but systemic longevity interventions remain preclinical and limited to delivery/safety.

resources.title: Synthetic Macromolecular Switches for Therapeutic Cells

nodes.title: Brain rejuvenation, microglia and neuroregeneration
nodes.summary: Neurons, synapses, myelin, microglia, neural stem cells, vasculature, and network integration in brain aging.
nodes.evidence_note: Separate cellular targets and replacement strategies are active, but restoring complex circuits and preserving functions requires tissue- and network-level validation.

resources.title: A Framework for Neural Organoids and Transplantation Studies
CRISPR Screens Reveal Regulators of Ageing in Neural Stem Cells

nodes.title: Cell, tissue and organ replacement
nodes.summary: Cell and tissue replacement, organoids, engineered grafts, stem-cell-derived organs, bioprinting and whole-organ engineering.
nodes.evidence_note: Transplantation and some cell therapies are clinically mature; fully engineered vascularized organs and extensive replacement of old tissue remain preclinical.

resources.title: MIT Tissue Engineering and Organ Regeneration
Toward Developing Human Organs via Embryo Models and Chimeras

nodes.title: Xenotransplantation
nodes.summary: Genetically modified animal organs as a source of replacement, including immune compatibility, zoonosis and longitudinal graft monitoring.
nodes.evidence_note: The first transplants of gene-edited pig organs were carried out in humans; durability, rejection, infection and trial-scale safety are still being investigated.

nodes.title: Biomarkers, aging clocks and multi-omics
nodes.summary: Measure biological aging, patient stratification and intervention response through molecular, functional, imaging and longitudinal data.
nodes.evidence_note: Many clocks predict age/outcomes, but responsiveness and surrogate validity for rejuvenation therapies still need system validation.

resources.title: Nonlinear Dynamics of Human Aging Multi-Omics

nodes.title: AI-driven longevity discovery
nodes.summary: AI for clocks, omics, target discovery, molecule/protein design, literature knowledge graphs and closed-loop experimentation.
nodes.evidence_note: AI accelerates individual steps, but does not automatically create clinical validity; prospective wet-lab and trial validation are mandatory.

resources.title: Creating an AI-First Drug Discovery Engine
Stanford AI and Computational Biomedicine Curriculum

nodes.title: Biostasis and organ cryopreservation
nodes.summary: Vitrification and reversible organ preservation as a bridge to transplantation/regenerative technologies rather than the proven revitalization of the whole person.
nodes.evidence_note: Progress has been made for cells, tissues and animal organs; reversible human whole-body or brain preservation has not been demonstrated.

nodes.title: Germline rejuvenation and intergenerational resetting
nodes.summary: Research on epigenetic resetting, oocyte/sperm aging, embryonic reprogramming and mechanisms that allow new generation to start from a young state.
nodes.evidence_note: Valuable for understanding rejuvenation mechanisms and reproductive aging; germline interventions carry special intergenerational and ethical risks.

resources.title: Mechanisms and Strategies for Rejuvenation through Epigenetic Reprogramming

nodes.title: Combination rejuvenation and whole-body integration
nodes.summary: The ultimate system goal is to safely combine measurement, damage repair, regeneration, cancer control and organ-specific interventions over time.
nodes.evidence_note: It is not an existing therapy. Combinatorial complexity, interactions, sequencing, monitoring and safety make this a separate system-engineering task.

resources.title: Hallmarks of Aging: An Expanding Universe

edges.rationale: Derivatives and integrals rely on functions and algebraic transformations.
Matrices and linear systems require solid algebra skills.
Probabilistic models use equations, functions, and graphs.
Differential equations are based on derivatives and integrals.
Algebra facilitates work with formal discrete structures.
Quantitative physics uses equations and graphs.
Stoichiometry, equilibrium, and kinetics require proportions and functions.
Organic chemistry involves bonds, acidity and thermodynamics.
The university course develops school ideas about the cell and heredity.
Molecular biology is more easily understood through the basics of chemistry.
Data analysis involves basic programming.
Algorithms are best learned after basic programming constructs.
Discrete structures provide a mathematical basis for algorithms.
Version control and environments are easier to understand after basic programming.
Data management follows from the requirements of verifiability of the study.
Biochemistry uses equilibrium, kinetics, and molecular interactions.
The structure of biomolecules and the mechanisms of enzymes require organic chemistry.
Biochemical processes are interpreted in the context of a living cell.
Molecular biology assumes basic knowledge of genes, proteins, and cells.
Cell biology deepens the introductory organization of the cell.
Genetics develops the foundations of heredity and evolution.
Epigenetics requires the mechanisms of expression and structure of the genome.
We need to distinguish between sequence change and genome regulation.
Physiology is based on cellular and organ biology.
Organ functions arise from the functions of cells and tissues.
Immunology requires cells, genetics, and molecular recognition.
Antigen receptors and signaling require a molecular base.
Microbiology uses cell biology and evolution.
Developmental biology requires cell fate and gene regulation.
Differentiation and morphogenesis rely on cellular processes.
Neuroscience requires cell biology and physiology.
Electrical signals and membrane potentials use physics.
Cancer biology involves cell cycle, death and signaling.
Tumors develop through mutation and clonal selection.
Tumor surveillance and immune escape require immunology.
Hallmarks describe violations of cellular mechanisms.
Aging is assessed at the cellular, tissue and system levels.
You need to understand the criteria of the causal hallmark and the limitations of the model.
Metabolism and redox are based on enzymes and energy.
Tissue metabolic effects depend on systemic physiology.
Proteostasis requires structure, folding and degradation of proteins.
Autophagy and lysosomes are cellular systems.
Oxidative phosphorylation and redox require biochemistry.
Mitochondrial dynamics and mitophagy occur in a cellular context.
Senescence requires cell cycle, stress responses, and signaling.
SASP and damage responses are regulated at the gene expression level.
ECM is viewed through cell-matrix interactions.
Stiffness and mechanotransduction use the mechanics of materials.
Drug targets and metabolism require biochemistry.
PK/PD and toxicity depend on organs and systems.
Dynamic pathway models use ODE and sustainability.
Biological networks are described by graphs.
Network nodes and edges must have a biological interpretation.
Power, uncertainty and testing are based on statistics.
Design implements the control of causal hypotheses.
Causal estimands require an understanding of design and bias.
Estimating causal effects uses statistical models.
Synthesis of evidence requires critical evaluation of research.
Meta-analysis uses effect sizes and uncertainty.
Trials are specialized experimental designs.
Clinical endpoints require an understanding of body functions.
Ethical risk is assessed in the context of scientific validity.
The technique must be based on an understanding of molecular mechanisms.
Wet-lab work requires controls and records.
Cell culture requires an understanding of cell states and environment.
Cellular assays use molecular readouts.
Measurable structures and markers must have cellular meaning.
Optics and fluorescence are based on the physics of light.
Animal studies require power, randomization, and control.
The model is selected for specific aging mechanism and outcome.
